chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, from Ahmad bin Muhammad, who said:

I said to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), 'I intend to go out to some of the mountains.' He said, 'The people will inevitably face turbulence in their year.' I said to him, 'May I be your ransom! When we sell to them with credit (nasi'ah), it yields more profit.' He said, 'So sell them with a delay of one year.' I said, 'With a delay of two years?' He said, 'Yes.' I said, 'With a delay of three?' He said, 'No.'
ai.seo_question: What is the maximum time limit for selling goods on credit according to Imam Al-Reza (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the jurisprudential boundaries of bay' al-nasi'ah (credit sale), establishing a maximum permissible credit term of two years to prevent excessive debt burden during periods of economic instability. The Imam’s rejection of a three-year delay highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on balancing commercial profit with social justice, ensuring that credit extension does not lead to unsustainable financial entanglement for the buyer.
